newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sanofi to launch Oscar de la Renta perfume in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Sanofi to launch Oscar de la Renta perfume in 1997.

text.p: Sanofi, the French health and beauty products group, next year will introduce a perfume for women under the Oscar de la Renta brand, Chairman Jean-Francois Dehecq said at a briefing for analysts on Tuesday.

"We are working on the launch of a new perfume in close cooperation with the designer Oscar de la Renta, who is very well regarded in the U.S.," Dehecq said. A company spokesman said the launch would take place in 1997.
Dehecq again attributed Sanofi's poor first-half performance in beauty products to weak economic conditions in Europe, which hurt most companies in the sector, he said.
He said December sales were particularly important to the company's full-year results. Dehecq said that he hoped the French transport strike would not drag on and disrupt the holiday selling season.
In addition, he said the increasing power of retail chains specializing in perfume was eroding margins.
"Here I want to be more selective as far as sales outlets are concerned," Dehecq said, complaining that parallel sales networks were counterproductive.
Dehecq recently decided to replace the head of the company's perfumes business because a restructuring was not proceeding fast enough.

Sanofi has grouped its beauty products around three creative centres, France, Italy and the U.S., with seven brands -- Yves Saint Laurent, Van Cleef & Arpels, Roger & Gallet, Nina Ricci, Krizia, Fendi and Oscar de la Renta.
The Yves Rocher brand is also used for a less exclusive line of products sold through direct marketing.

Dehecq dismissed a suggestion by one analyst that the company might sell the beauty products division and concentrate on drugs. He said there were many synergies between the two lines of business, as other groups were only recently discovering.
Sanofi is majority-owned by oil group Elf-Aquitaine
